entries.name: Great tit
behaviour: bold and acrobatic, hangs upside-down to work bark
hoards hundreds of seeds for winter
learns its way around bird-feeders and larders within hours

voxel_model.pattern: black head with white cheeks, green back, yellow underparts with a black tie

entries.notes: The most familiar mixed-woodland songbird; a permanent fixture of gardens, feeders and the lunch-hour scaffold. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Blue tit
behaviour: dances along the thinnest twig tips looking for caterpillars
squeezes through tiny holes to nest, happiest in small-entrance boxes
forms mixed flocks with great tits in winter

voxel_model.pattern: cobalt cap and wings, white face, yellow underparts

entries.notes: Smaller, bluer, friskier cousin of the great tit; a tiny blue spark that migrates through every coppice in winter drafts. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Common chaffinch
behaviour: delighted in winter stubble and hedgerow flocks
song ends in a rattling flourish, unmistakable from February
hop-walks rather than perches when feeding on the ground

voxel_model.pattern: male pink breast, grey-blue cap, bold white wing bars

entries.notes: Europe's most numerous songbird; the February first-song date is a classic spring-marker for any in-game calendar. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Song thrush
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern birds winter south
behaviour: repeats each musical phrase two to four times, unlike any other thrush
smashes snail shells against a particular 'thrush anvil' stone
spots worms by a head-cocked tilt from mid-lawn

voxel_model.pattern: brown upperparts, cream breast densely spotted with black arrowheads

entries.notes: The repetitious virtuoso; the snail-anvil habit gives the world generator an excuse to scatter cracked shells beneath a favored stone. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Eurasian wren
entries.migrates: partial in far north; otherwise sedentary
behaviour: ticket-plump, tail cocked straight up, dashes through the undergrowth like a brown flicker
males build several dome nests and let the female choose
sings with explosive volume far out of proportion to its 10-gram body

voxel_model.pattern: fine dark barring on warm brown, cocked tail, thin white brow

entries.notes: The loudest voice per gram in the wood; its tail-cock and round-body silhouette make it instantly readable as a voxel bird. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Eurasian nuthatch
behaviour: the only bird that climbs down trunks head-first with equal ease as up
wedges a nut into bark and hacks it open with hatchet strokes
plasters mud around the nest hole rim to fit the entrance

voxel_model.pattern: slate-blue back, orange flanks, black eye-stripe, short tail

entries.notes: The axe-beak of the oak trunk; mud-mortar nest-rims and head-down climbing are two signature behaviours worth scripting. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Common nightingale
behaviour: sings 200+ distinct phrases, at night without pause, for hours on end
skulking, rufous, best heard at dusk from dense bramble
males arrive weeks before females and stake claims by song

voxel_model.pattern: plain rufous-brown, red-brown tail flashed when cocked

entries.notes: The unseen virtuoso; a night-time audio cue rather than a sight. Declining in Western Europe with the scrub it needs. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Common wood pigeon
behaviour: rocks back and forth walking, deep purr of cooing in the canopy
display flight: stiff clap-and-glide waltz with whistling wings
feeds in huge agricultural flocks; a serious crop pest in autumn

voxel_model.pattern: grey body, white neck slashes, white wing bars in flight

entries.notes: The clattering plank of the suburban canopy and the stubble field; clap-fly display is its unmistakable signature. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Eurasian woodcock
entries.migrates: winter visitor from the north and east
behaviour: probes deep litter with a bill tip packed with nerve endings
freezes dead still, eyes offering a near-360 degree watch
roding display at dusk: twittering spiral flight over treetops

voxel_model.pattern: mottled rufous, black banding, eyes set high and far back

entries.notes: The forest's ghost-probe; legendary for freezing underfoot a metre from a boot. Roding flights at dusk are an April soundscape essential. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Middle spotted woodpecker
behaviour: forages high in old oak, hornbeam and elm branches, rarely drumming
short, fine bill for gleaning bark crevices rather than hacking
sedentary; presence maps old-growth oak exactly

voxel_model.pattern: red crown, pink vent, no black moustache stripe, streaked flanks

entries.notes: Europe's old-oak specialist; almost never recorded in Britain, a living index of ancient continuous woodland. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Common shrew
behaviour: racing heartbeat forces it to eat almost constantly between bouts of sleep
tiny but fierce; corners and kills mice larger than itself
high-pitched squeaking, echo-locates with ultrasonic ticking

voxel_model.pattern: tricolored coat: dark back, warm brown flanks, pale belly

entries.notes: The furious knot of speed under the leaf-litter; mostly important because owls, and owls because pellets. Keep heartbeat and squeak as ambient flavour.

entries.name: Pygmy shrew
behaviour: Europe's smallest terrestrial mammal, lighter than a 20-cent coin
so tiny it can walk on a postage stamp and back again in seconds
feeds more continuously than even the common shrew

voxel_model.pattern: warm brown above, pale ash below, two-tone like its larger cousin but miniature

entries.notes: The smallest land mammal in Europe; a reminder that a 'small' voxel is the right place to put the entire ecology of the leaf-litter.

entries.name: European mole
behaviour: shovels 20 m of new tunnel a day, pushing molehills like periscope tops
blood nearly saturated with oxygen for hours at a time underground
lives on worms alone and near-starves within 24 hours without one

voxel_model.pattern: velvet charcoal fur, pink star nose, huge shovel forelimbs

entries.notes: The landscape engineer under every lawn; molehill-churn is free terrain decoration and its tunnel-network makes a lovely underground structure.

entries.name: Field vole
behaviour: makes runways through grass that native runners use for foraging
population cycles every three to four years with explosive irruptions
bites and holds when captured, stronger than expected

voxel_model.pattern: grizzled brown above, pale grey below, blunt nose

entries.notes: The granary of the raptor world; every third or fourth year the 'vole year' decides whether nest boxes produce chicks. Its runways are worth rendering.

entries.name: European water vole
behaviour: dives with loud plop from the bank into slow water
feeds on a liking spot at the water's edge, eating in a messy pile
latrines of clipped stem-ends mark owned banks

voxel_model.pattern: uniform deep chocolate, blunt chubby face, small rounded ears

entries.notes: 'Ratty' from The Wind in the Willows; decimated in Britain by American mink and wetland draining, recovering through reintroduction.

entries.name: Harvest mouse
behaviour: the only truly climbing mouse in the wild — prehensile tail grips reed stems
weaves a fist-sized ball nest a metre up in standing grass
most abundant after wet years and rank meadow edges

voxel_model.pattern: tawny-gold above, white belly, tiny glinting eyes

entries.notes: The smallest mouse in Europe; its ball-nest woven among reeds is a jewel for the nature-education spots in the game.

entries.name: Yellow-necked mouse
behaviour: an acorn-caching dynamo; thousands per autumn, half forgotten, half planted
yellow collar across the chest sets it apart from the wood mouse
home ranges shift to the mast source year to year

voxel_model.pattern: chestnut back, white belly, bold yellow-buff neck collar

entries.notes: The oak woodland's forester; pairs with the jay as one of the two great vectors replanting European oak after the ice.

entries.name: Edible dormouse (fat dormouse)
behaviour: hibernates seven months straight and nearly doubles in weight before sleeping it off
Romans kept them in clay gliraria jars and fattened them on acorns and wine
clump together in nest boxes; a box may hold thirty in October

voxel_model.pattern: silver-grey, bushy white-tipped tail, black eye-ring

entries.notes: Britain's biggest rodent, an introduced classic of the Chilterns; the historic 'glires' of Roman feasts and field-murals alike. Hibernation weight-gain is a brilliant power mechanic, if wanted.

entries.name: Garden dormouse
behaviour: the most carnivorous dormouse — takes chicks and lizards alongside fruit and beetles
glows pink under ultraviolet, skin and nose shining greenish in UV light
Near Threatened across Europe; the Alps and Bavarian Forest are its last strongholds

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with a black mask, tail ending in a white brush

entries.notes: The outlaw dormouse; its UV fluorescence is a once-in-a-generation discovery for a curiosity-hunter character. A declining flagship of southern woodland.

entries.name: European polecat
behaviour: anal-gland musk when cornered — 'stinker' is its oldest English name for good reason
lives masked like a cartoon bandit, white-marked over brown
fierce rabbit hunter and an occasional henhouse raiding menace

voxel_model.pattern: dark mask over pale face, pale guard-hair fringe along the back

entries.notes: The wild ancestor of the domestic ferret; once persecuted to near-extinction, now rebounding with rabbit conservation and legal tolerance.

entries.name: Common pipistrelle
entries.migrates: largely sedentary; a few long-distance strays
behaviour: echolocates at ~45 kHz with short, brick-dry clicks one octave above human hearing
roosts in bat boxes, roof spaces and hollow trunks; colonies swap boxes seasonally
frozen mid-air hovers in oak-to-oak foraging sallies over water and lanes

voxel_model.pattern: small russet body, broad rounded wings

entries.notes: The sound of a British summer evening resolving into ticks; its 45 kHz call is the prime signal for a bat-detector mechanic.

entries.name: Brown long-eared bat
behaviour: ears nearly as long as the body; hears a moth flapping its wings in the dark
gleans motionless prey directly off leaves and bark without echolocation — the quietest bat hunt
folds its huge ears like a fan when flying at speed for aerodynamics

voxel_model.pattern: rabbit-eared silhouette, folded wings above the body

entries.notes: The whisper-bat; hunting by listening instead of echolocation is unique enough to carry an entire stealth-hunting game loop.

entries.name: Common lizard (viviparous lizard)
behaviour: gives live birth — the lizard that refused Europe's egg model
freezes then bolts in jerky dashes between sun-bathing logs
northern range holder; the only reptile above the Arctic Circle

voxel_model.pattern: olive-brown, flanks with dark net-like vermiculation

entries.notes: The little log-basking lizard most people mistake for an escapee newt; ovoviviparity and Arctic reach are its headline facts.

entries.name: Slow worm
behaviour: a legless LIZARD, cousins to all lizards — it flicks a forked tongue but has eyelids and can blink
basks beneath warm stones and compost, then vanishes like a snake
autotomises its tail when seized; the name fragilis means brittle

voxel_model.pattern: slow glassy sheen, female with flank streaks, limbless gloss

entries.notes: The snake that blinks; educating the player's eye with eyelids-versus-spectacle is the cheapest false-ID lesson in the game.

entries.name: Great crested newt
entries.migrates: spring migration to breeding pond, autumn return
behaviour: males grow a jagged breeding-season crest and flash a fiery orange belly
tail-flick courtship waves scent across the pond
EU-protected; a single pond can block a housing development

voxel_model.pattern: black-brown back, warty skin, vivid orange belly with black blotches, jagged crest

entries.notes: Europe's dragon-in-miniature; crest, belly-flash and tail-wave make the breeding season the single most cinematic amphibian event in the wood.

entries.name: Common toad
entries.migrates: spring explosive migration to ancestral pond
behaviour: warty skin exudes bufotoxin; the pattern is a walking DO-NOT-EAT sign
annual toad road crossings are mass-migration events where hundreds cross a lane in one night
home range: the same shady corner for a decade

voxel_model.pattern: olive-brown warted skin, amber eyes with horizontal pupils

entries.notes: The millstone of the allotment; 4000-8000 eggs per string and a mass migration to the birth-pond each spring are the two set-piece behaviours to model.

entries.name: European tree frog
behaviour: adhesive toe pads let it cling to glass-smooth leaves, inverted or upright
males inflate a vocal sac the size of the head and produce a deafening night chorus
colour shifts green to brown with humidity and mood

voxel_model.pattern: bright leaf-green back, dark flank stripe, yellow-green vocal sac

entries.notes: The emerald whistle of the pond-edge; the loudest amphibian relative to body size in Europe, and declining with wet-meadow drainage.

entries.name: Common cockchafer (May beetle)
behaviour: drunken bumbling flight and a loud buzz on warm May evenings
the C-shaped white grubs tunnel and eat grass roots for three years below ground
mass emergence years used to defoliate whole orchards — 'Maikäferflug' in German almanacs

voxel_model.pattern: chestnut-brown elytra, black head, cream fan-clubbed antennae

entries.notes: The Maikäfer of every European May; its three-year grub cycle underground gives the game a ticking subterranean clock and a visible above-ground bloom.

entries.name: Seven-spotted ladybird
behaviour: reflex-bleeds yellow alkaloid droplets (reflex bleeding) when handled
aggregates in mass overwintering clusters under tree bark and in sheds
a living pesticide: one adult eats thousands of aphids a season

voxel_model.pattern: bright red elytra with seven round black spots in 3-1-3 arrangement

entries.notes: The gardener's mascot; mass-hibernation aggregates of hundreds beneath loose bark are an easy interact-to-reveal moment.

entries.name: Peacock butterfly
entries.migrates: adults hibernate in tree hollows and sheds
behaviour: eyespots on all four wingtips startle birds into missing the body
hibernated adults emerge on the first warm February day, months before other butterflies
caterpillars strip stinging nettles wholly bare in communal webs

voxel_model.pattern: brick-red grounds, one huge blue-ringed eyespot per wingtip

entries.notes: The four-eyes that overwinters as an adult in a shed loft; the first butterfly of the year and the herald of nettle patches.

entries.name: Common glow-worm
behaviour: the flightless female perches in grass and glows green-blue to pull winged males out of the dark
glow is cold light, ~96% efficient — biochemistry outshines every bulb on Earth
two-year larval stage is a snail-hunter that injects paralysing venom

voxel_model.pattern: trilobite-like larva body, greenish-glow tip in females

entries.notes: The living lantern of June evenings; harvesting glows would make a fortune — which is why one must not. A perfect light-source that cannot be crafted.

entries.name: Grove snail (white-lipped banded snail)
behaviour: textbook shell-polymorphism: yellow, pink or brown with 0-5 dark bands, endlessly variable
bird-drop predation sorts the colour mixes locally, the classic Cain-Sheppard experiment
seals itself behind a chalky epiphragm for winter or drought

voxel_model.pattern: globose banded shell, white lip, a living genetics demo

entries.notes: The shell whose bands taught population genetics; scattered shells under a thrush's anvil should be a real find on the forest floor.

entries.name: Garden cross spider (European diadem spider)
behaviour: spins a perfect orb each evening; hub marked with a white cross of guanine dots
wraps prey in silk, bites it into a paste, and drinks it like soup
females balloon young away on silk parachute threads in autumn

voxel_model.pattern: brown-orange body with a white cross of five spots on the abdomen

entries.notes: The classic orb-web spider holding the eight-pointed cross; an autumn garland for lamp posts and a sample biologist specimen.

entries.name: Leopard slug
behaviour: two mates suspend themselves head-down on a glistening rope of mucus and curl together in mid-air
stretches to 20 cm fully extended; ridges and dark spots earn its name
races snails to baited traps where hedgehogs are too big to follow

voxel_model.pattern: grey with dark spots and ridges, tail striped like a leopard's

entries.notes: The mid-air mucus ballet; the single most astonishing reproductive moment in any temperate woodland, worth rendering as an autumn cutscene.

entries.name: Death-watch beetle
behaviour: males tap their heads on timber with a loud tick; the female answers within two seconds
larvae chew inside fungal-rotten oak beams for up to ten years before emerging
the 'death-watch' of folklore — a tapping heard by candlelight at the sickbed
sounds: tick-tick tapping of head on wood

voxel_model.pattern: cylindrical dark-brown with patches of grey hair, concealed head

entries.notes: The ghost in the oak beam; a tapping sound source with folklore weight, perfect for old-building horror set-dressing. Feed it on the dead oak the designer should already be placing.

entries.name: Rosalia longicorn (alpine longhorn beetle)
behaviour: cobalt-blue on sunlit beech bark — effectively invisible, effectively camouflaged, stunning when found
antennae twice the body length in males, same length in females
chirps by scraping rear legs against elytra; three-year larva in the bark of old beech

voxel_model.pattern: sky-blue with fuzzy thorax, black spots, powder-blue antennae

entries.notes: The beetle collectors' holy grail; Vulnerable, protected across Europe, emblem of Danube-Ipoly National Park — a genuinely rare find worth a discovery event.

entries.name: European grayling
entries.migrates: short upstream spawning runs in spring
behaviour: sail-like dorsal fin spreads into a living semaphore when excited or alarmed
iridescent scales shift from chromium to purple depending on water clarity
indicator of pristine, oxygen-rich streams; vanishes where banks silt up

voxel_model.pattern: silvery flanks, purple-and-black dorsal sail, thyme-scented flesh

entries.notes: The lady of the stream; thyme-scented and sail-finned, tied to flies-and-nymphs fly-fishing fantasy — a premium fishing target for the game.

entries.name: White-clawed crayfish
behaviour: creamy underside and pale claw joints under a dark shell
hiding beneath bank stones by day, patrolling at night
exterminated at plague-fronts by crayfish plague carried in by signal crayfish

voxel_model.pattern: dark olive-black shell, pale (white) underside and claw lower edge

entries.notes: Europe's last native crayfish, collapsing before signal crayfish and their plague; the game's waterways need both, plus an invaded frontier.
